title: Identifying Substances
subject: Science
source: NYSED 2024 Grade 5 ELS Released Items, Questions 19-23
directions: Base your answers to questions 19 through 23 on the information below and on your knowledge of science.

intro.html: Students conducted experiments to identify unknown substances using properties of known substances. During these experiments, appropriate safety equipment was used and safety procedures were followed.
Through experimentation, the students observed that an unknown substance was a fine, white powder that reacted to vinegar, was soluble in water, and did not conduct electricity.

particles.html: The models below represent the number and arrangement of particles in a sample of water and a sample of sugar.

particles.alt: Two boxes and a key. The box labeled Water has 9 water particles (circles) at the bottom, a row of 5 above a row of 4. The box labeled Sugar has 7 sugar particles (black triangles) at the bottom, a row of 3 above a row of 4. The key shows that a circle is a water particle and a black triangle is a sugar particle.

minerals.html: Students were then provided four minerals and completed certain tasks to identify the properties of each mineral. The table below shows the observations for four of the five properties that the students observed. The photographs below show the response of a strong magnet when brought close to each mineral.

minerals.alt: Four photographs of minerals, each with a small magnet drawn above it and a label over the magnet. Muscovite Mica: label reads Magnet not attracted, and the magnet hangs above the mineral. Talc: label reads Magnet not attracted, and the magnet hangs above the mineral. Calcite: label reads Magnet not attracted, and the magnet hangs above the mineral. Pyrite: label reads Magnet attracted, and the magnet is tilted down onto the mineral.

calcite.html: The students then placed calcite onto a glass dish and placed it on a scale. Using an eye dropper, ten drops of vinegar were placed on top of the calcite and the total mass was recorded.
Bubbles formed on top of the calcite and the total mass was recorded again.
The diagrams and observations below represent the experimental setup and the observations made by the students.

Calcite Experiment Results
Calcite with VinegarCalcite after Response to Vinegar
Mineral Observations:
— Surface texture smooth
— Total mass of vinegar, calcite,and glass dish is 19.65 grams.
— Clear/white color
Mineral Observations:
— Bubbles formed
— Surface texture slightly rough where vinegar is applied
— Total mass of vinegar, calcite, and glass dish is 18.75 grams.
— Clear/white color

rocks.html: The students were then given three different rock samples, labeled A, B, and C, to test with vinegar. The table below shows the results of the tests.

items.stem: Place a checkmark (✓) in the table below to indicate the identity of the unknown substance. [1]
items.adapted: No wording change. On screen, selecting a box in the table places the checkmark in it, so the printed direction still works. Only one box can be checked at a time.

items.stem: Which model best represents the number and arrangement of the water and sugar particles after the sample of sugar was poured into the sample of water and mixed?

options.alt: Model A: a box with 8 water particles (circles) and 7 sugar particles (black triangles) in three rows at the bottom. Circles and triangles take turns in every row.

Model B: a box with a top row of 5 water particles (circles) over a bottom row of 3 water particles and 4 sugar particles (black triangles) taking turns. 8 water particles and 4 sugar particles in all.

Model C: a box with a top row of 3 sugar particles (black triangles), a middle row of 3 water particles (circles) and 2 sugar particles taking turns, and a bottom row of 4 water particles. 7 water particles and 5 sugar particles in all.
Model D: a box with 9 water particles (circles) and 7 sugar particles (black triangles) in three rows at the bottom. Circles and triangles are spread through every row.

items.stem: Indicate if each mineral is magnetic by typing Yes or No in Student Data Table 1. [1]
items.adapted: "writing Yes or No" changed to "typing Yes or No" because students type into the Magnetic cells of the table.
items.explanation: Note: Allow credit if a student writes something other than yes or no that correctly identifies the mineral is magnetic or non-magnetic.

items.stem: A student makes a claim that a new substance was formed when vinegar was added to calcite. Which statement can be used as evidence to support this student’s claim?
options: The calcite changed color after the vinegar was added.
The vinegar droplets caused the calcite sample to melt and lose mass.
Bubbles formed after the vinegar was added to the calcite.
The surface texture of the entire calcite sample changed after the vinegar was added.

items.stem: Based on the results shown in Student Data Table 2, explain why rock A is most likely made of the mineral calcite. [1]
rubric: Allow 1 credit. Acceptable responses include, but are not limited to:
Bubbles formed on the surface of Rock A so it probably has calcite in it, the other minerals would not form bubbles.
Rock A bubbled when vinegar was added just like calcite.
items.exemplar: Rock A bubbled when vinegar was added just like calcite.
